title: Thirty FIRs
logline: Branch A, the night of the doors. Nandini chains her own prisoner to her wrist because he is the only man Imlipur will open a door for, and between twenty past one and ten to ten the two of them turn thirty refused complaints into thirty FIRs on a desk made of their two arms, until the DSP's car pulls up at the thana with the man named in all thirty as chief guest.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast and same actors as the Hinglish cut; 'ji', 'sahab', 'madam', 'Amma', 'arre', 'thana' and 'FIR' kept as spoken in India.
script_note: Indian English adaptation of script.hi.json: same beats, line ids, speakers and order; only text, emotion_tags and target_seconds differ.

characters.name: Nandini Joshi
characters.role: LEAD. Sub-Inspector, Imlipur thana. Tonight she takes her own prisoner door to door, chained to her, to register thirty FIRs before ten.
characters.look: Indian woman, 28, tall, lean, very straight-backed. Medium-brown skin, oval face, straight thick black eyebrows, a firm mouth that rarely smiles. Low ponytail with a clean centre parting, no loose strands. No make-up, no jewellery, no watch. Approved force uniform, crisp: sandy khaki shirt with two buttoned chest pockets, full sleeves, dark teal epaulettes with TWO off-white bars, white lantern patch on each upper sleeve, khaki trousers, black belt with the handcuff pouch (empty this episode) on her right hip, black shoes, blue ballpoint pen. NO HELMET in this episode (D-016 direction 19). STATE: her LEFT wrist is handcuffed to Nirala's RIGHT wrist from b1 to the end; in a front two-shot she stands picture-left. The green FIR register is under her right arm between doors and open across their two forearms at a door; she writes with her right hand. From b7 a grey cardboard token is in her left chest pocket.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, late twenties, clear mid-range voice. Indian English with a neutral, educated small-city north-Indian accent; no British or American colour. Keeps 'madam', 'ji', 'FIR' (read as letters, F-I-R). Quick, clipped. Under pressure quieter, slower, more exact, never louder. Dry, not sarcastic.

characters.name: Sudhir Nirala
characters.role: Second lead. The fake Inspector, now her prisoner, and the only person the town's doors open for.
characters.look: Indian man, 40, slight and short, narrow sloping shoulders, thin neck. Light-brown skin, long narrow face, large earnest eyes, neat black pencil moustache. Home-stitched copy of the force uniform, over-starched and ONE SIZE TOO BIG: shoulder seams drooping, sleeves to his knuckles, collar standing off his neck, belt tail hanging loose. Teal epaulettes with three off-white bars, lantern patches. THE ONLY PEAKED CAP IN THE SERIES, khaki with a teal band and a shiny black peak, dead level. The palm-wide blank brass medal on its maroon-and-off-white ribbon above his left chest pocket (on all episode). Brown leather holster on his right hip, EMPTY with the flap buttoned flat: the wooden revolver was sealed as case property in s2a01 b2 (S4 confirmed: empty, flap buttoned flat, s2a01 b2 to the end of branch A). STATE: his RIGHT wrist is cuffed to her LEFT; picture-right in a front two-shot. The red cloth-tied file is clamped under his LEFT arm all episode. At a door he holds the open tin ink pad in his free LEFT hand; the pad lives in his right trouser pocket between doors. A few spare grey cardboard tokens on their own short string in his left trouser pocket, carried from habit; the lobby string stays on its nail.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Male, forty, light careful tenor. Careful, slightly old-fashioned Indian English as learnt from manuals, with a small-town north-Indian accent; no British or American colour. No contractions ('do not', 'it is'); 'kindly'. English police terms pronounced with great care. Unhurried, courteous, never raises his voice, never jokes: the comedy is that he means it. Under pressure more formal and quieter, sentences shorter. Says 'madam' at the end of sentences.

characters.name: Pushpa Kumari
characters.role: Head Constable. Minds the real thana through the night; names the arrivals at the end.
characters.look: Indian woman, 50, short and solid. Wheat-brown skin, round face, sharp small eyes over round steel-rimmed spectacles worn low. Grey-streaked bun with TWO STEEL KNITTING NEEDLES crossed through it. Approved force uniform with ONE off-white bar, lantern patches. Plum-purple hand-knitted cardigan, open, two sagging pockets, orange wool in the right pocket. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, fifty, low, dry, even alto. Plain, unhurried Indian English with a small-town north-Indian accent; no British or American colour. Short sentences. Never surprised. Under pressure slower and more exact. Always 'madam', 'DSP sahab'; DSP read as letters.

characters.name: Anil Rathore, DSP
characters.role: The DSP. First time on screen (b12), stepping out of his white car. No line in this episode.
characters.look: Indian man, 48, tall and lean, upright. Short silver-grey side-parted hair, trimmed grey moustache, rimless rectangular spectacles. Sharply pressed force uniform, teal epaulettes each with ONE BROAD off-white band (no bars, no stars), lantern patches, polished brown belt, slim brown leather cane under his LEFT arm. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Silent in this episode. (Male, late forties, bright, quick, clipped baritone; fluent officer's Indian English, no British or American colour.)

characters.name: Balram 'Bhaiyaji' Thakur
characters.role: Antagonist, named in all thirty FIRs. Arrives in the DSP's car as chief guest (b12). No line in this episode.
characters.look: Indian man, 45, broad and solid, thick neck, big square hands. Thick black hair combed straight back, full black moustache, an unhurried closed-lip smile. Spotless white cotton kurta, sleeves pushed up, white pyjama, brown sandals. Heavy gold watch on his LEFT wrist. Dark sunglasses pushed up on his head, never over his eyes. Fat ring of godown keys on his RIGHT index finger. A marigold welcome garland round his neck (prop, D-016 direction 19). No religious marks, no party colours.
characters.voice_note: Silent in this episode. (Male, mid-forties, warm, low, smiling voice; soft, hospitable Indian English.)

characters.name: Ramsevak
characters.role: The first complainant, whose door shut at the end of s2a01. In this episode a hand and a voice only.
characters.look: Never a face in this episode: a thin older man's hand on the edge of a door opened a hand's width, the end of a shawl. The same hand comes down on the ink pad in b4.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Tired, flat, older male, small-town north-Indian accent. One line, half-recognising the knock.

characters.name: Shanti Devi
characters.role: Complainant. A one-shot face (b6 shot 1 only); her second line plays over an insert of her hands.
characters.look: Small woman, 65, white hair in a loose bun, green cotton sari, a steel tumbler in her hand.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Warm, scolding, grandmotherly. Simple Indian English with a strong small-town Hindi accent; keeps 'arre' and 'ji'. No British or American colour.

characters.name: Mukesh
characters.role: Complainant. A one-shot face (b9 shot 1 only).
characters.look: Young man, late 20s, checked shirt, a folded stamped receipt held up in his fist.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Young male, stubborn, hurt; small-town north-Indian English accent. One line.

characters.name: Door four (voice)
characters.role: A complainant behind a door held on its chain (b10). A hand and a voice; never a face. Not a fourth face.
characters.look: A hand holding a wooden door on its iron chain latch, a hand's width open.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Middle-aged, tired, sharp, not unkind; small-town north-Indian English accent; gender is the casting director's call. One line.

location: real_thana (b1, b2, b12); lane_doorway, the one door plate re-dressed per door (b3 to b7, b9 to b11); crossing_stall (b8). No crowd anywhere: the town is hands, thumbs and voices.
time_of_day: Night into morning: 1:20 a.m. in the lockup to 9:55 a.m. in the thana doorway. Night blue with the wall lamp lit (b3 to b6), the lamp going out as the sky greys (b7), dawn at the stall about 6 a.m. (b8), warm morning light from about 7:30 (b9 to b12).

beats.action: OPENS ON A SOUND, over black: a key grinding in the rusted lockup lock (the first 0.6 s of the silence). Real thana, night, one tube light, 1:20 a.m., twenty minutes after s2a01 ended. Shot 1 (insert, the hook image, lands by about 2 s): the barred lockup door standing open; Nandini's hand snaps one ring of the steel handcuffs shut on her OWN LEFT wrist; the chain runs picture-right to the other ring, still locked on Nirala's RIGHT wrist. Shot 2 (two-shot in the open cell doorway, she picture-left, he picture-right, chain between): she pushes the red cloth-tied file at him and he clamps it under his free left arm; cap level, medal on. l01 starts over shot 1; cut to shot 2 on 'Not yours. Mine.', which plays to his face. No helmet.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] I need bail, Nirala ji. Not yours. Mine. Let's go.

beats.action: RUNNING GAG, FIRST TIME. The same room, towards the front doorway; Pushpa at her side table, knitting in her lap, the zero-crime shield on the wall behind the SHO's empty desk. Shot 1 (two-shot, front, she picture-left, he picture-right, the green register under her right arm): passing Pushpa he snaps a salute with his right hand and Nandini's chained left arm is yanked up with it: the chain pulled TAUT, her hand dangling from the cuff, fingers loose, her face startled. One image: two arms in the air, one taut chain. l02 plays over shot 1. Shot 2 (Pushpa single): her eyebrows up over her low spectacles, she lays the needles down and returns the salute gravely, once, to both. The silence after plays over shot 2.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [quietly] Kindly excuse me, madam. It is habit.

beats.action: About 1:30 a.m. The SAME door that shut at the end of s2a01 (Ramsevak's): same door colour, the bicycle leaning by the step, as in s2a01 b11, wall lamp lit, night blue. Shot 1 (the door, the pair as backs at the frame edges; one state): the door open a hand's width, a thin hand on its edge, the end of a shawl, no face; Nirala's free left knuckles still raised by the wood. The knock is sound only, his own knock, and plays with the door opening in the silence before. l03 comes from behind the door. Shot 2 (two-shot in the lamplight, she picture-left, he picture-right): l04. Second framing of shot 2 (1.2x, wrists up): on l05 he lifts their joined wrists into the lamplight, the chain lit. The door opens fully on his last word (sound).

lines.speaker: door1_man
lines.text: [quietly] Nirala ji?

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] Ramsevak bhai. Madam is the real one. [quietly] The fake was me.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [earnest] If you do not believe me, see the handcuffs.

beats.action: The same doorstep. There is no table. Shot 1 (tight two-shot): the green register lies open across their two chained forearms, her left and his right side by side, the chain under the book; she writes with her right hand; he holds the open tin ink pad in his free left hand, the red file still clamped under that arm. Ramsevak's hand (no face) comes down on the pad. l06 plays over shot 1. Shot 2 (insert, top-down on the page): the first thumbprint on a ruled page; overlay ov_fir_numbers '1' in the margin. The silence after plays over shot 2.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] FIR number one. Thirty by ten.

beats.action: The lane between doors, night, walking out of step. Shot 1 (two-shot, front, she picture-left, he picture-right, the chain jerked taut between them): the register open in the crook of her right arm; he leans in to read her entry upside down. l07 and l08 play over shot 1. Shot 2 (second framing of shot 1 at 1.2x, on her hand and the page): l09 and l10; in the silence after, her pen is caught mid-stroke striking the line she wrote: she bristles, then changes it.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] The section comes first, madam. The date after.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [sharply] I topped the Academy.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] And I failed nine times.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] So I had to read the syllabus more times than you.

beats.action: About 3 a.m. A second door on the same plate, re-dressed: a different door colour, a brass water pot on the step, lamp lit. Shot 1 (Shanti Devi single, her ONLY shot: in the half-open door, steel tumbler in hand, disbelieving): l11. Shot 2 (two-shot, she picture-left, he picture-right): l12, he answers her gently. Shot 3 (insert, hands only): Shanti's thumb comes off the ink pad in Nirala's left hand and her steel tumbler points at the chain; l13 plays over it, her voice from off the face. Shot 4 (Nandini close, a reframe of shot 2 at 1.3x or less): l14, and in the silence after, her first almost-smile of the series, the corner of the mouth only.

lines.speaker: door2_woman
lines.text: [excited] Nirala ji is fake? Arre, he is the one who found my goat!

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] The goat was real, Amma. The uniform was fake.

lines.speaker: door2_woman
lines.text: [sharply] Such a good man, and you have tied him up?

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [deadpan] Other way round, Amma. He tied me.

beats.action: The night as objects, not people; no new face. Shot 1 (insert, the silence before plays over it alone): a page filling with thumbprints; overlay ov_fir_numbers '11' in the margin. Shot 2 (the lane, wider, the pair small at a door, the wall lamp just gone out, the sky paling from blue to grey): out of habit Nirala's free left hand holds out a grey cardboard token on its string, from his left trouser pocket, to a complainant's hand (hand only); l15. Second framing of shot 2 (1.3x on the hands): Nandini's right hand takes the token back; l16, and she pockets it in her left chest pocket.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] Token eleven.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] No more tokens, Nirala ji. FIR number eleven.

beats.action: Dawn at the crossing stall, about 6 a.m., grey-gold light, the gate arm up, the track empty, the hanging bulb off. The tea-stall keeper is hands on the kettle only. Shot 1 (insert, the silence before plays over it): two glasses of tea, one chain: his right hand lifts his glass and her chained left hand rises with it; her right hand holds her own glass to her lips, timed to his. Shot 2 (two-shot on the stall bench, she picture-left, he picture-right, the register on her knee, the red file under his arm): l17 plays over shot 2. Second framing of shot 2 (1.3x on Nandini, the chain at the frame edge): l18 plays over it.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [quietly] In my register, there was only comfort. In yours, there is punishment.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Without your register, mine would still be empty today.

beats.action: THE TURN. About 7:30 a.m., warm morning light, lamp off. A third door on the plate: a new door colour, a tin bucket upturned by the step. Shot 1 (Mukesh single, his ONLY shot: in the doorway, checked shirt, the folded stamped receipt held up in his fist): l19. Shot 2 (two-shot favouring Nirala, he picture-right and sharp, she picture-left and soft, the chain between): l20, played straight and slow, no music sting. Shot 3 (insert, hands only): Mukesh's thumb going onto the ink pad in Nirala's left hand, the receipt crushed in the same fist; l21 plays over it, Nirala's voice from off the frame, and the silence after holds on it.

lines.speaker: door3_man
lines.text: [sharply] This receipt has Nirala ji's own stamp on it!

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [quietly] That stamp I made myself, Mukesh. I cut it from rubber.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [earnest] Do not put your trust in that. Put it in her.

beats.action: THE DOOR NIRALA CANNOT OPEN; HER WIN. About 8:30 a.m., full morning light. A fourth door on the plate: a new colour, the end of a charpai against the wall. Shot 1 (the door, one state; the silence before plays over it): the door open a hand's width and stopped on its iron chain, a hand on its edge, no face; Nirala's free left knuckles still raised by the wood. The knock (the same knock as b3) and the door stopping on its chain are sound only. l22 from behind it. Shot 2 (two-shot): Nirala looks down at his own cuffed right wrist and says nothing; she steps in front of him; l23. Shot 3 (Nandini single, front, his sleeve and the chain at the frame edge): she lifts the chain into the light herself with her own left wrist; l24 and l25. Under the end of l25, insert: the hand slides the door chain off and a thumb comes out towards the ink pad. Nirala has no line in this beat.

lines.speaker: door4_voice
lines.text: [sighs] A man who is in handcuffs himself, how will he save us, Nirala ji?

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] The handcuffs are mine.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] And last night, your grain went out right in front of me.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Lodge the FIR. So it never goes again.

beats.action: The clock against them. Shot 1 (insert, low on the lane): two pairs of feet hurrying, hers in black shoes, his in too-big ones, at last in step, the chain swinging at the top of frame; l26. Shot 2 (two-shot at the last door, about 9:50, the door just shut behind them; front, she picture-left, he picture-right, the register shut under her right arm): both saluting the house, the chain hanging SLACK in a loop between the raised wrists, her chained hand flat at her own brow, her face composed. The register cover's thump is heard before l27; l27 and the silence after play over shot 2. No overlay: the thirty is spoken in l27. GAG PAID: against b2's taut chain and dangling hand, she salutes with him by choice.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [sharply] Nine thirty. Twenty-seven.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] Thirty. Ten minutes to spare.

beats.action: ENDING, SPOKEN. Five to ten by the wall clock (hands only, no numerals). The real thana dressed for the press: a table with a cluster of microphones facing camera, the zero-crime shield polished, the cloth banner behind (overlay ov_press_banner); no audience in frame. Shot 1 (Pushpa single at the microphone table, the banner behind her, looking past the camera at the yard; this shot establishes the dressed room): the car-door clunk lands at the head of shot 1, before l28; l28. Shot 2 (through the front doorway, past the backs of Nandini and Nirala standing in it, still chained, the register under her right arm, the red file under his left): a white car door open in the yard, the DSP stepping out, cane under his left arm; from the other door, Bhaiyaji in the marigold garland, keys on his finger, smiling; two sheet faces only, the pair are backs. l29 plays over shot 2. Shot 3 (insert, held through the silence after): Nandini's right hand tightening on the green register.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [calm] DSP sahab is here, madam.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [calm] And with him, the chief guest... Bhaiyaji.

sfx_notes: Beds (one ambience per location, from the series library): real_thana night, tube-light hum and a slow ceiling fan; lane night, crickets and a far-off goods train, changing at b7 to first birds and at b9 to a quiet morning town (a distant scooter, a pressure-cooker whistle far away; never voices, never a crowd); crossing_stall dawn, a kettle on a coal stove and the track ticking.
b1: the key grinding in the rusted lock opens the episode over black; then the dry ratchet of the cuff closing on her wrist, close and exposed.
b2: a chain clink as both arms go up; Pushpa's needles set down on the table.

b3: NIRALA'S KNOCK, one fixed rhythm (two slow, one quick), made once and reused in b10, then the door opening a hand's width, all inside the 1.5 s silence before l03; an iron chain latch sliding; a wooden door opening on his last word.
b4: the tin lid of the ink pad; a soft thumb press; pen scratch.
b5: a chain clink on every out-of-step stride; the pen strike in the silence.
b6: a steel tumbler set down on a stone step after l13.
b7: (shot 1 only, the page insert) thumb presses and page turns in a loose rhythm; the wall lamp's buzz dying as it goes out; the first bird.
b8: kettle bubbling, two glasses set down, a chain clink each time his glass lifts. Nothing loud under l17 or l18.
b9: paper unfolding as he holds up the receipt; nothing at all under l20 and l21 but the bed.
b10: the same knock as b3 (two slow, one quick); the door stopping hard on its chain, both inside the 1.5 s silence before l22; the chain sliding off under the end of l25. No effect under l22.
b11: two sets of hurried footsteps, out of rhythm then falling into one; a door shutting; the register cover thumping shut at the head of shot 2, before l27; one chain clink on the salute.

b12: a car idling in the yard, a car door opening (one clean clunk) at the head of shot 1 (the Pushpa single), BEFORE l28, sandals on gravel. The bed and the music duck under l28 and l29; no effect sits on l29, so the cliffhanger stays fully clear. Hold on the tube-light hum and the fan over the final insert.
music_note: Series theme set (bed, tension, sting, ending), instrumental. No music in b1 and b2: the key, the cuff and the chain carry them. From the first knock (b3) a light, warm small-town bed, plucked strings and a soft clarinet, playful under the salute and the goat, ducking under every line. It thins to almost nothing for b9, the turn, and comes back warmer under the dawn tea in b8 and the morning doors. From b11 a ticking pulse joins as the clock runs; it lifts on the salute by choice. On the car door in b12 the pulse stops dead; one low sustained tension note sits under Pushpa's two lines, ducked well below the voice, and a short sting lands on the final insert of her hand, then cut to black.
ending_question: The man named in all thirty FIRs has arrived as the DSP's chief guest: will the DSP take the register, or bury it, and Nandini with it?
writer_notes: S5 English adaptation of script.hi.json revision 2 (26 Nov). Sources: that script, the bible's per-character 'en' speech notes (Nandini keeps 'madam', 'FIR', 'ji'; Nirala manual-learnt English, no contractions, 'kindly'; Pushpa plain short sentences, 'madam', 'sahab'), D-016 and D-0M2. Same beats b1 to b12, same lines l01 to l29, same speakers and order; beat actions, sfx_notes and music_note are unchanged except that b1's cut cue now quotes the English words ('Not yours. Mine.'). Every emotion tag is kept as in the Hindi; no tag was changed.

Length: spoken targets 99.6 s (Hindi 108.1 s); 20 speaker changes at 0.3 s = 6.0 s; silences 13.9 s, unchanged; total 119.5 s. Targets are set to the English length at roughly 3.2 to 3.5 syllables a second, about 10 to 12 characters a second without tags, kept slow because the Gate 0b v4 takes ran 20 to 60 per cent over their targets. If the English takes run 30 per cent over, the total reaches about 149 s; the trim order in script.hi.json applies: (1) l03 and its two speaker changes; (2) 'Let's go.' from l01; (3) the b7 silence to 1.2 s; (4) l17 to 'My register only had comfort. Yours has punishment.'; (5) the b6 and b9 silences. Never cut b10, l26, l27 or the b12 ending. Nothing was padded.

Per-line length against the Hindi target: every line is within 15 per cent, most 8 to 12 per cent shorter. Closest to the limit: l01 (5.0 against 5.8, 14 per cent short; its pauses after 'Nirala ji' and 'Not yours' carry the cut to shot 2), l06 and l15 (12 per cent short). No line runs longer than its Hindi line, so no shot needs extending for English by target times; real takes decide (D-014 rule 6).

Adaptation choices, intent unchanged: l01 'bail' keeps the joke that the jailer needs the surety. l04 'Madam is the real one' for 'ये असली हैं', since 'she' at a door reads cold for Nirala. l05 'see the handcuffs' (Indian English for 'look at'). l07 'The section comes first' in his manual register. l08 to l10 become 'I topped the Academy.' / 'And I failed nine times.' / 'So I had to read the syllabus more times than you.': the ninth-fail joke lands on 'more times than you'. l11 adds 'Arre' as her natural carrier and 'he is the one who' for the disbelief. l13 is reordered so 'tied him up' sits last and feeds l14. l14 'Other way round, Amma. He tied me.' carries the Hindi reversal ('बाँधा इन्होंने है') in English word order; it ends on 'me' as the Hindi ends on 'मुझे'. l17 keeps Nirala's formal 'there was / there is' parallel. l19 'own stamp' carries the stress of 'निराला जी की मोहर वाली'. l21 keeps the 'that / her' parallel of 'उस पर / इन पर'. l22 keeps the Hindi's third person ('A man who...') addressed to Nirala, in Indian English topic-first order. l24 'your grain' matches s2a01's eight hundred sacks. l25 'Lodge the FIR' is the Indian police phrase. l26 'Nine thirty' for 'साढ़े नौ'. l29 keeps the pause before the name.

Read-aloud checks for S10: FIR (l06, l16, l25) and DSP (l28) must be read as letters. 'Nirala ji', 'Ramsevak bhai', 'Amma', 'Arre', 'sahab' and 'Bhaiyaji' must keep Indian pronunciation, not an anglicised one. Verify-group tags as in the Hindi: [earnest] (l05, l21), [deadpan] (l14); S10 swaps for [calm] or [quietly] if ignored. Short turns l03 'Nirala ji?' and l15 'Token eleven.' need extra takes. If l11 [excited] reads as glee, S10 may use '[sharply] Nirala ji is fake? [excited] Arre, he is the one who found my goat!'. No whisper anywhere; the cliffhanger l29 is calm, unfiltered, with the bed ducked.

Story checks: no recap, no narrator; the cuff on her own wrist lands inside 2 s with l01 over it; target and deadline spoken in l06 and paid in l26 and l27; b9 played slow; b10 is her win with Nirala silent; the last line names the arrival and does not answer ending_question.

Not verified: the JSON was not parsed by a tool and lengths were counted by hand (this session has Read, Write, Edit, Grep and Glob but no shell); no line has been voiced or timed; the adaptation has not been reviewed by the critic.
